scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what's going on here. So, there's me, my best friend G, and my twin sister. G and I have been best friends since kindergarten, which is a really long time. My sister and G have always been pretty close too, and they've had this "thing" going on for a long time. They finally started dating when we were 17, and everything was great for about a year. But then, G cheated on my sister. I found out about it and told my sister, even though G begged me not to. That made both of us really mad, and we didn't talk for a month and a half. That was super weird for me because G is like my brother, and not having him around felt really strange. Eventually, G invited me on his family's ski trip to make amends. I went, and after that, I forgave him and let him back into my life because it was just too weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened, and he even cried because he felt so bad. I've only seen him cry once before in my whole life. Now, G and my sister broke up right after she found out he cheated, and they're still not speaking. My sister is making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13-year friendship over this. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it, but I'm not going to let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and felt like shit about it, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall, which is a different college in a different state than where my sister is going. So, none of this is going to be something we even think about when we're living in different places. Am I the asshole here? Alright, so I need to figure out if I'm being an asshole. Let's break this down. First, I need to understand what makes someone an asshole in this context. An asshole is someone who is selfish, inconsiderate, or unreasonable. So, am I being selfish by continuing the friendship with G despite my sister's feelings? Or am I being reasonable by valuing a long-term friendship? I think it's important to consider both sides. On one hand, my sister feels hurt and betrayed by G's actions, and she's upset that I'm still friends with him. She might feel like I'm not taking her side or that I'm dismissing her feelings. On the other hand, I value my friendship with G, and I see that he's genuinely sorry for what he did. I also think that friendships can survive mistakes, especially when there's genuine remorse. Another thing to consider is the impact on all parties involved. My sister is clearly hurt, and she's expressing that by making me feel bad. But I'm also hurt because I lost a month and a half of communication with G, and it was really hard for me. I also had to deal with the guilt of telling my sister, even though I thought it was the right thing to do. There's also the aspect of whether continuing the friendship is fair to my sister. She might feel like I'm not respecting her boundaries or that I'm not standing up for her. But I also think that friendships can be separate from romantic relationships. Just because G hurt my sister doesn't mean he can't still be my friend, especially if he's taking responsibility for his actions. I also need to think about the future. We're all going to different colleges, so this situation might not even come up again. It might be something we can leave in the past and move on from. But for now, it's causing tension between me and my sister, which is really hard. Another point is whether I'm being inconsiderate of my sister's feelings. She's going through a tough time, and she might feel like I'm not supporting her by still being friends with G. But I also need to support myself and my own feelings. I don't want to lose a friendship that's been important to me for so long, especially when G has shown that he's sorry. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can maintain the friendship with G but also support my sister in her healing process. It might be challenging, but it's worth trying to find a balance where both my sister and G feel respected and heard. In the end, I think it's important to communicate openly with both my sister and G. Maybe if we all talk about how we're feeling and what we need, we can find a way to move forward that works for everyone. But I also know that communication can be really hard, especially when emotions are running high. So, am I the asshole? I don't think so. I'm trying to value my friendship with G while also respecting my sister's feelings. It's a tough situation, and there's no perfect solution, but I'm doing my best to navigate it.
